note: LATER BOUNDS, NOT 1904 WITNESSES. The two c. 1923 views are the earliest dated photographs of the Glessner frontages in the repository, nineteen years after the scene. No. 2 (Prairie Avenue) shows, from the house outward, a pale walk laid in jointed slabs, a paved crossing from the front door over the grass to the curb, a grass parkway with a young tree, a pale curb jointed in straight lengths, and a smooth pale roadway. No. 3 (18th Street) shows a grass strip at the wall, the same jointed pale walk, a grass parkway and the same curb, with the roadway beyond. Both are consistent with a cement walk and a stone (or concrete) curb and cannot tell the two curbs apart at this resolution; neither can say what was there in 1904. No. 1 (1963) shows 18th Street patched asphalt with no parkway left on the Prairie side.
what_it_supplies: the arrangement of walk, parkway and curb on both Glessner frontages c. 1923, and their appearance: jointed pale slabs, grass, a pale jointed curb
a later bound (c. 1923) on the reconstructed walk, curb and parkway materials
